findings.Quote: the only thing either of them had left to spend on dignity
findings.Note: Tells the reader what the gesture means instead of trusting the image; abstract 'dignity' currency reads as an inserted aphorism rather than earned emotion.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause or replace with a concrete detail showing the cost of leaving food behind.

findings.Quote: which was the thing he should have been thinking about, and wasn't
findings.Note: Explicit authorial flagging of foreshadowing/irony — tells the reader what to notice instead of trusting the scene.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause and let the omission speak for itself, or show a beat of hesitation instead.

findings.Quote: The room's temperature changed before he finished the sentence.
findings.Note: stock tension-shorthand metaphor, vague and unearned as physical description
findings.Fix: replace with a concrete, specific sensory beat — someone's stance shifting, a sound cutting off, a hand moving

findings.Quote: It was something else, something neither of them had a name for yet
findings.Note: Vague, hand-wavy emotional gesture — asserts unnameable significance without giving the reader any texture to grasp; borders on pseudo-profound filler.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete physical detail (a twitch, a held breath, a specific expression) that lets the reader assign the meaning.

findings.Quote: the one that didn't know yet what it was standing on top of
findings.Note: Vague foreshadowing metaphor that tells us doom is coming without grounding it in anything concrete — reads as ominous filler rather than earned dread.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a specific, concrete detail that implies the coming trouble.

findings.Quote: every open channel in him agreed, past any argument he could have raised, that this was the thing everyone had always been going on about
findings.Note: universal-truth quip / telling-not-showing the emotional payoff instead of rendering it
findings.Fix: cut the generalization and let the preceding concrete details (laugh, ribs, warmth) carry the beat

findings.Quote: the node opened for him the way a lock opens when someone who's been listening for years finally hears the right click
findings.Note: Overextended simile that tells us he's skilled via ornate comparison rather than showing it; the 'listening for years' clause doesn't track literally with a lock/click mechanism.
findings.Fix: Cut to something plainer: 'the node opened like it had been waiting for him.'

findings.Quote: understood the door was not going to open for him — not through anything he had — and he was right
findings.Note: Redundant confirmation ('and he was right') after already stating the man understood; tells us the outcome twice, deflating tension.
findings.Fix: Cut 'and he was right' or cut the 'understood' clause and just show the man's action/inaction.

findings.Quote: Reza had stood in a doorway and made his body the only door that mattered.
findings.Note: Purple, self-consciously poetic phrasing that doesn't hold up literally — a body isn't a door, and the metaphor strains for profundity rather than clarifying the image.
findings.Fix: Ground it concretely: 'Reza had filled the doorway so nothing could pass but him.'

findings.Quote: What he couldn't stop looking at, later, was how little it had cost him to do it.
findings.Note: tells the reader the emotional weight directly rather than dramatizing it, a summary-aphorism closing beat rather than shown reaction
findings.Fix: replace with a concrete physical/behavioral detail showing his unease, or cut the line and let the prior image carry it

findings.Quote: and the smile was real, and then it was over and there was nothing to put after it
findings.Note: telling-not-showing the emotional beat instead of dramatizing it; 'nothing to put after it' is a vague abstraction standing in for concrete detail
findings.Fix: show the silence via action/dialogue rather than narrating its shape

findings.Quote: the grin that arrived before the thought
findings.Note: Stock construction for describing an instinctive facial expression, generic in cyberpunk/literary prose alike.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific physical beat unique to Reza.

findings.Quote: neither of them named the thing that had gone out of the world.
findings.Note: Vague, inflated abstraction ('the world') standing in for a specific emotional loss — tells rather than shows what actually ended.
findings.Fix: Specify what gesture/ritual is gone, or cut the generalizing clause.

findings.Quote: nothing out here had ever been painted on purpose
findings.Note: Vague purple flourish that gestures at meaning without delivering concrete image — reads as a stand-in for actual description.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a specific visual detail (e.g., rust streaks, tagged plywood) that grounds the grayness.

findings.Quote: climbing until it stopped being visible and then climbing further into a sky
findings.Note: clunky mechanics — 'a sky' reads as an article error and the clause is redundant after 'stopped being visible'
findings.Fix: "climbing until it stopped being visible into the sky" or similar tightening

findings.Quote: The bowls were the kind of cheap that meant the broth was real, because nothing else was.
findings.Note: Aphoristic construction that reads as a clever-sounding non-sequitur rather than a clear observation; the logic (cheap=real broth because nothing else was) doesn't quite parse literally.
findings.Fix: Cut the 'because' clause or replace with a concrete detail, e.g. 'The bowls were the cheap kind, but the broth tasted real.'

findings.Quote: an apron that had been white once and had reached its current color through honest work
findings.Note: Cute editorializing phrase ('honest work') tells us how to feel about her rather than showing; slightly precious for the otherwise flat register.
findings.Fix: e.g. 'an apron gone gray with grease and years' — drop the moralizing tag.

findings.Quote: She watched them the way you watch the weather.
findings.Note: Second-person 'you watch' aphorism is a familiar device for stoic-observer characterization.
findings.Fix: Rephrase in third person and more specific: 'She watched them the way she'd watch a cloud bank — not interested, just tracking.'

findings.Quote: a name like that just piles up, the fifth or sixth time you hear someone use it
findings.Note: Vague explanatory aside that gestures at meaning without landing a clear image or logic — reads as filler musing.
findings.Fix: Cut or sharpen to a concrete beat, e.g. state plainly it was a nickname earned from an old wound, no explanation of how names 'pile up.'

findings.Quote: the way you read a page you've read many times and find it hasn't changed
findings.Note: Reaching literary simile that doesn't clarify the actual action (sizing up strangers for augments) and feels like inserted 'writerly' flourish.
findings.Fix: Replace with a direct, physical description of her scanning gaze.

findings.Quote: Something moved in her face, a thin flicker that wasn't quite a smile.
findings.Note: Vague telling-through-description; 'something moved in her face' is a stock hedge for unreadable expression without giving concrete detail.
findings.Fix: Name the specific muscle or feature, e.g. 'One corner of her mouth twitched, then stopped.'

findings.Quote: She was on to the next bowl.
findings.Note: Flat closing line functioning as a thematic stamp ('life goes on') rather than earned observation.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete action detail specific to Scraps, not a generic indifference beat.

findings.Quote: which was not a name
findings.Note: cute aside that tells rather than shows, slightly smug authorial voice intruding
findings.Fix: cut the aside or ground it in a concrete detail (e.g., a name clearly borrowed from a product label)

findings.Quote: That had seemed like a good idea eight seconds ago.
findings.Note: wry retrospective narration undercuts the immediacy of an unfolding violent grab, tonal wink out of step with the danger
findings.Fix: cut the aside or compress it into action rather than commentary

findings.Quote: Reza wasn't moving like a man who'd made a mistake.
findings.Note: Tells the reader how to interpret his state rather than showing it through concrete detail; slightly abstract framing for an otherwise physical beat.
findings.Fix: Cut the line and let the stillness of his hands carry the meaning.

findings.Quote: which turned out to be the right forty percent
findings.Note: Cute authorial wink that undercuts tension with a wry aside rather than staying in the scene's urgency.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause or replace with a plainer statement of the result (e.g., 'enough of it').

findings.Quote: running south, because south was away
findings.Note: Faux-profound tautology that reads as a quip rather than grounded geography or motivation.
findings.Fix: Specify an actual reason or landmark for the direction instead of the circular justification.

findings.Quote: Tavi's lungs were doing something he wouldn't have called breathing.
findings.Note: vague evasive phrasing that tells rather than shows the physical state
findings.Fix: Tavi's lungs hitched, ragged, refusing to fill.

findings.Quote: the haze thick and brown and full of things that weren't their problem
findings.Note: the personified 'things that weren't their problem' is a cute abstraction that doesn't specify anything concrete
findings.Fix: the haze thick and brown, carrying smells and noises they didn't stop to name

findings.Quote: the grin was back, but it was sitting on top of something that hadn't been there this morning
findings.Note: vague abstraction stands in for a concrete observed detail, telling rather than showing what changed in Reza
findings.Fix: specify the physical tell, e.g. 'the grin was back, but his jaw was tighter than it had been this morning'

findings.Quote: The number sat there, patient and real.
findings.Note: Personifying the number as 'patient' is a slightly strained abstraction for a purely visual fact (digits on a display).
findings.Fix: The number didn't change, no matter how long he looked at it.

findings.Quote: because the Gray Zone had seen worse
findings.Note: Editorializing aphorism that tells us about the setting's character rather than showing it through the specific action.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause or replace with a concrete detail of what she'd seen.

findings.Quote: with the reckless certainty of two nineteen-year-olds holding the biggest number either of them had ever owned
findings.Note: Slightly telling summary of their emotional state rather than dramatized behavior; borders on explaining the scene's own stakes.
findings.Fix: Let the dialogue and pace of planning carry the recklessness without the label.

findings.Quote: how the whole warm weight of it in his pocket wanted to stay whole
findings.Note: Personifying the money's 'want' is a soft abstraction that slightly overreaches for a physical credstick in a pocket.
findings.Fix: how much he wanted to keep it whole

findings.Quote: Tavi's thumb moved over the display without deciding anything.
findings.Note: A thumb moving 'without deciding anything' is a slightly vague gesture meant to convey internal conflict but reads as inert rather than charged.
findings.Fix: Tavi's thumb hovered over the display, and he still said nothing.

findings.Quote: His hands had stopped shaking somewhere between the squat and here, and he hadn't noticed when.
findings.Note: Stopped-shaking-hands-as-relief/aftermath is a familiar post-heist beat shorthand.
findings.Fix: Anchor to a more specific physical detail unique to Tavi.

findings.Quote: It was enough to stop.
findings.Note: Flat, abstract statement that tells us the significance of the number instead of showing why it matters to Tavi specifically.
findings.Fix: Give a concrete referent — enough to stop what, exactly, in his life.

findings.Quote: He was not good at finishing this kind of sentence, and didn't pretend to be.
findings.Note: Telling-not-showing his discomfort rather than letting the broken dialogue itself carry it; redundant after the visible stammer.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence and let the trailing dash and gesture do the work.

findings.Quote: real work going on behind it
findings.Note: Vague filler phrase gesturing at interiority without specifying what the 'work' is — a placeholder rather than an image.
findings.Fix: Specify what's visibly working — e.g. a tightening jaw, a recalculation in his eyes — or cut.

findings.Quote: which was also an answer
findings.Note: Stock construction ('silence is also an answer') used often enough to register as reflexive rather than earned.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete physical beat showing Tavi's non-answer.

findings.Quote: something went through Tavi's chest, quick and warm, before he had a word for it
findings.Note: Vague interiority stand-in for a specific emotion; tells rather than shows.
findings.Fix: Name the physical specificity or cut to action instead of naming an unnamed feeling.

findings.Quote: Reza went first, because he was always going to go first.
findings.Note: Circular pseudo-profound phrasing that asserts inevitability without giving the reader a reason.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete trait or motive: e.g., 'Reza went first, the way he always volunteered for the dark rooms.'

findings.Quote: His face in the mirror looked the same as before, which felt like a small, specific lie.
findings.Note: Tells the emotional beat abstractly rather than showing what's dissonant; 'small, specific lie' is a vague abstraction standing in for concrete detail.
findings.Fix: Anchor the lie in something physical: e.g., 'His face looked the same, but he kept expecting it not to.'

findings.Quote: Something moved across Reza's face that wasn't quite a smile.
findings.Note: Vague non-description that dodges specificity — tells us an expression occurred without conveying its character.
findings.Fix: Specify the expression, e.g., 'The corner of Reza's mouth twitched, tight, gone.'

findings.Quote: let the wrongness pass through him like weather. Present. Specific. Temporary.
findings.Note: Fragment sequence reads as a stylistic tic asserting profundity rather than showing sensation; the weather simile is generic.
findings.Fix: Cut the three-word fragment run and let the sensory detail carry the meaning.

findings.Quote: something that hadn't been there before, something that would stop what it was built to stop
findings.Note: Vague, circular phrasing ('stop what it was built to stop') tells rather than shows and is nearly tautological.
findings.Fix: Specify what the hardware does or cut the second clause.

findings.Quote: the clinic was supposed to be clean, Ozzie had said the clinic was clean
findings.Note: Redundant restatement of the same fact twice in one clause reads as a drafting error rather than intentional emphasis.
findings.Fix: Cut the duplicate: 'the clinic was supposed to be clean, Ozzie had sworn to it.'

findings.Quote: the particular quality of the silence that followed told him someone was standing in it, listening for the same thing he was listening for
findings.Note: Overwrought abstraction ('quality of the silence') tells the reader what to feel instead of grounding it in a concrete sound or absence of sound.
findings.Fix: Replace with a specific auditory detail, e.g., no footsteps, no floorboard creak, just held breath.

findings.Quote: He had the pistol out before he finished the thought, and it was loaded, and that was all he had.
findings.Note: The closing clause 'that was all he had' is a vague, filler-profundity tag that doesn't add concrete information.
findings.Fix: Cut the trailing clause or replace with a concrete detail (e.g., one magazine, no backup).

findings.Quote: looked back at Reza with an expression
findings.Note: Vague, telling-not-showing; dodges specifying the reaction it's building toward.
findings.Fix: Name the expression: unease, hesitation, or whatever is intended.

findings.Quote: the way a person smiles when they've decided to be present
findings.Note: Slides into abstract aphorism rather than a concrete observed detail, softening the showing established just before it.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory clause and let the described smile stand alone.

findings.Quote: a texture that landed in his chest before it reached his lips
findings.Note: purple sensory image that doesn't quite hold up to literal scrutiny — a texture felt in the chest before the lips is more assertion of intensity than a coherent sensation
findings.Fix: ground it in a more specific physical effect, e.g. 'a texture that hit his chest like a second pulse'

findings.Quote: the pull was an answer to something he hadn't known he'd asked
findings.Note: vague pseudo-profound abstraction standing in for concrete sensation
findings.Fix: replace with a specific physical/emotional beat rather than a riddle-phrase

findings.Quote: In that one motion she was somewhere else entirely, three transactions further down her day.
findings.Note: Abstract quantifier ('three transactions') gestures at precision but doesn't actually clarify anything concrete about her state.
findings.Fix: Cut to a specific image of what she's now doing/thinking instead of the vague count.

findings.Quote: She had heard boys say it before.
findings.Note: Tells us her jaded reaction rather than showing it through action or detail; reads as flat narratorial summary dropped into an otherwise scenic beat.
findings.Fix: Show the dismissal physically (a shrug, a specific memory-flash) rather than stating the generalization.

findings.Quote: held opinions about footwork the way other men held religion
findings.Note: Simile aims for wit but is a fairly stock 'X the way men hold religion' construction that reads as a filler quip rather than earned voice.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete, specific detail about his footwork obsession instead of the comparison.

findings.Quote: like he'd grown there
findings.Note: Stock rooted-in-place simile for stillness/steadiness.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile; state the fact plainly: 'still standing in the doorway when the count ran out.'

findings.Quote: pulling a thread because pulling felt good and he wanted to know how far it went
findings.Note: Vague sensory abstraction stands in for concrete detail; tells rather than shows what the pleasure/skill actually consisted of.
findings.Fix: Anchor with a specific action or system he cracked.

findings.Quote: Neither of them minded yet. Neither had needed to be apart.
findings.Note: Sets up foreshadowing via flat statement rather than dramatized tension; borderline telling-not-showing.
findings.Fix: Could stay as is for brevity, but consider grounding it in a specific moment instead of narratorial assertion.

findings.Quote: the room was dark in a way the lights being off couldn't explain. Erased-from-the-record dark.
findings.Note: Abstract, self-consciously clever phrasing that asserts atmosphere without grounding it in a concrete sensory detail.
findings.Fix: Anchor it: 'The cameras still ran, but the feed showed an empty room, always had.'

findings.Quote: did what Breckenridge had taught him, which was nothing complicated
findings.Note: Mentor-taught-him-well beat is a stock action-scene device, delivered with a slightly too-cute understatement.
findings.Fix: Cut the aside or make it more specific to what was taught.

findings.Quote: the jaw made a sound
findings.Note: Vague euphemism stands in for a concrete detail, undercutting the otherwise precise physical choreography.
findings.Fix: Specify the sound or cut the sentence.

findings.Quote: said "Rampart," like she was testing whether the word fit. It did.
findings.Note: Tells the reader the word 'fits' rather than showing why via detail, a small telling-not-showing shortcut for characterization payoff.
findings.Fix: Let the fit be implied by Reza's demeanor or cut the confirming line 'It did.'

findings.Quote: the noise Reza had made in that stairwell was exactly the confirmation the node's owners needed that someone was hunting their traffic
findings.Note: Convenient exposition-dump explaining the whole mechanism in one breath reads as telling rather than dramatized consequence.
findings.Fix: Split into two beats or let this surface through dialogue/action rather than narrator summary.

findings.Quote: He said it like weather.
findings.Note: Stock simile for flat affect, seen often in noir/cyberpunk delivery of bad news.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile or replace with a more specific, unexpected comparison tied to Ozzie's character.

findings.Quote: Tavi had stood at a terminal and made himself into something the cameras couldn't find a reason to remember.
findings.Note: Abstract, tells the reader Tavi's function rather than showing the mechanism, echoing the prior line's structure mechanically (parallelism used as a crutch).
findings.Fix: Make the image specific — what he actually did to the footage/logs.

findings.Quote: Nobody had trained them to be opposites. It had just come out that way.
findings.Note: Reads as a tidy aphoristic capstone, a universal-truth-flavored summary line rather than earned insight.
findings.Fix: Cut, or replace with a concrete detail that shows the difference in practice.

findings.Quote: and it was a good board, and their rate began, slowly, to climb
findings.Note: Flat, redundant restatement of information already delivered in beat 1 (Ozzie's prediction that rate would climb), adding no new texture.
findings.Fix: Trim to avoid repeating the same beat, or specify what 'good board' concretely means.

findings.Quote: the Substrate's cleanup nano losing its argument with whatever Ashgrave was cooking in the secondary refinery
findings.Note: personifying nano as losing an 'argument' is a slightly strained metaphor that draws attention to itself without adding clarity
findings.Fix: e.g. 'the cleanup nano failing to mask whatever Ashgrave was cooking in the secondary refinery'

findings.Quote: feeling — briefly, and without permission — the particular lightness of a job with only one weight to carry
findings.Fix: tighten to a single concrete image rather than abstract 'lightness'/'weight' metaphor stacking

findings.Quote: a level up from anything he and Reza had ever touched
findings.Fix: clarify the metaphor's literal grounding (level of what — money, class, access) so it doesn't read as vague status-speak

findings.Quote: Reza takes the right, so you take the left, and you stop even looking that way.
findings.Note: Shifts into present-tense second-person mid-narration, an abrupt mechanical hiccup that reads as instructional rather than remembered reflex.
findings.Fix: Reza took the right, so you took the left, and you stopped even looking that way.

findings.Quote: The crack was internal, a sound he felt more than heard, low in his chest.
findings.Note: Slightly overwrought phrasing for a quick action beat; 'felt more than heard' edges toward stock sensory-paradox description.
findings.Fix: The crack was internal, low in his chest.

findings.Quote: The guard was big and trained and had four inches on him, and none of it mattered
findings.Note: Telegraphs the outcome via flat assertion rather than letting the fight choreography demonstrate it.
findings.Fix: Cut the summary clause and let the elbow strike carry the point.

findings.Quote: This was the rest of that feeling — the weight when it wasn't there, and the open place it left on the right.
findings.Note: Abstract phrasing obscures rather than clarifies the physical/emotional referent; reads as vague rather than precise.
findings.Fix: Anchor to a concrete referent, e.g. name what's missing (the person, the limb, the object) so 'open place' lands.

findings.Quote: the Substrate's nano to start its low, warm argument with the swelling
findings.Note: Personified-tech metaphor ('argument') is a bit cute and softens the visceral pain beat with whimsy.
findings.Fix: Consider a more clinical or sensory verb than 'argument' to keep tone consistent with the flat, controlled voice.

findings.Quote: the one they'd bought from a gray-market Splicer in the Bloom Quarter when they were nineteen and thought hardware would fix whatever they were
findings.Note: the vague 'whatever they were' gestures at depth without specifying anything, a soft-focus dodge
findings.Fix: name the actual thing they thought it would fix, or cut the clause

findings.Quote: the front edge of the old signal, the one that had never once needed explaining
findings.Note: tells us the signal's history and significance rather than letting the gesture itself carry it
findings.Fix: trust the gesture; cut the explanatory clause

findings.Quote: He thought about saying something true and didn't.
findings.Note: generic withheld-truth beat, tells the reader there's unspoken depth without specifying any content
findings.Fix: gesture at what the true thing might have been, even obliquely

findings.Quote: Reza said "same time next week" and meant it, and Tavi said "yeah" and meant something slightly different
findings.Note: 'meant something slightly different' is vague hand-waving over the actual emotional content
findings.Fix: specify what Tavi's 'yeah' actually meant, even briefly

findings.Quote: She said it the way she said everything — with a courtesy that was also the whole sentence.
findings.Note: Abstract, self-consuming aphorism that describes nothing concrete about how she speaks; reads as a placeholder for characterization rather than actual voice.
findings.Fix: Cut, or replace with a concrete detail of her tone/word choice.

findings.Quote: He said "same time next week" and didn't mean it, and Tavi said "yeah," and they both knew.
findings.Note: 'they both knew' is a telling tag that asserts mutual understanding without showing it; slightly deflates the scene's restraint.
findings.Fix: End on the dialogue beat without the summarizing tag.

findings.Quote: the chemical thread underneath that he still couldn't name after two years of trying
findings.Note: Vague sensory filler that gestures at mystery without giving the reader anything concrete; reads as atmosphere-padding rather than earned detail.
findings.Fix: Name a specific failed guess (e.g., 'solvent, maybe, or burnt sugar gone wrong') to ground it.

findings.Quote: the particular stillness of people being told something they're afraid to ask her to repeat
findings.Note: Overwrought abstraction stating an inferred emotional state rather than showing it through action or detail.
findings.Fix: Cut to a physical beat: 'the two kids not moving, not asking her to say it twice.'

findings.Quote: their eyes held a beat longer than a stranger's should
findings.Note: Stock 'meaningful eye contact' phrasing used to signal recognition/tension.
findings.Fix: Specify what about the look was wrong—e.g., 'the thin one's eyes tracked him past the point where strangers stop looking.'

findings.Quote: worn to the shape of his palm and no one else's
findings.Note: Reaches for intimacy/possession but is a slightly inflated claim for a pocketed grip—reads as trying too hard for characterization via object.
findings.Fix: Simplify: 'worn smooth from his grip alone' or cut the qualifier.
